title: --out aliasing the input path (e.g. ./x.json vs x.json) with --overwrite overwrites the turns file
evidence:
writeTranscriptQaReport guards only `outPath === opts.inputPath` (string equality), so any alias of the input defeats it. Repro (cwd packages/ai, node from codex runtime): `cp exact.json alias.json; node --import tsx ../../scripts/qa/transcript-qa-report.ts <S>/alias.json 20 --out <S>/./alias.json --overwrite` printed `PASS in=2 out=2 clamped=0 dropped=0 -> <S>/./alias.json`, exit 0; alias.json now begins `{
  "verdict": "PASS", "failReasons": []` i.e. the input turns file was replaced by the report (sha256 before 9386aef9600e6281...). Same string-equality form (`--out <S>/alias.json`) is correctly refused. Same hole for relative-vs-absolute, backslash vs slash, case differences on Windows, symlinks. Violates 'never modifies the input'.
fix_direction: Compare path.resolve() (and realpathSync / case-folded on win32, or stat dev+ino when both exist) of outPath and inputPath before writing; add a regression test using `./`-prefixed and absolute-vs-relative forms.
